info.name: TradeLedger API
info.description:
Personal crypto trade journal and portfolio dashboard, synced automatically from the Bitunix exchange.

**Read-only against the exchange.** TradeLedger never places, modifies or cancels an order.

## Quick start

1. Select the **TradeLedger - Local** environment (or edit the collection variables).
2. Run **Auth > Login**. The token is saved to `{{token}}` automatically by a test script, and every other request inherits it from collection-level Bearer auth.
3. Run **Accounts > Create account** to get an `{{accountId}}`, then work through the other folders.

Requests that create something save the new id into a collection variable (`accountId`, `tradeId`, `planId`), so the folders can be run top to bottom, or with the Collection Runner.

## How a trade reaches the journal

A closed Bitunix position becomes a journal row on its own. The mechanical half (prices, quantity, leverage, fees, funding, PnL) comes from the exchange; the subjective half (strategy, mental state, mistakes, rating) is supplied through `PATCH /api/trades/{id}/journal`.

All enums are sent and returned as strings, e.g. `"side": "Long"`, `"kind": "ExternalWallet"`.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Sign in and inspect the current user. Public signup is deliberately absent: the owner account is seeded at startup from configuration.

request.description:
Returns a bearer token for every other endpoint, and saves it to `{{token}}`.

Unknown email and wrong password give the same 401 on purpose, so the endpoint does not confirm which addresses exist.
The signed-in user plus their journal baseline: starting balance, journal start date, default risk per trade and display time zone. Everything is stored UTC; the time zone is for display only.

item.name: Accounts
item.description: Venues where value lives, and their encrypted exchange credentials.

request.description:
Every venue where value lives: Bitunix futures, Bitunix spot, external wallets and purely manual venues.

Credentials are never returned, only the last four characters of the API key so you can tell keys apart.

exec: // Names are unique per user, so keep re-runs from colliding (409).

request.description:
Registers a venue and saves the new id to `{{accountId}}`.

Bitunix futures and Bitunix spot are separate accounts. `trackedFrom` is the date the backfill stops walking back to.

`kind`: ExchangeFutures, ExchangeSpot, ExchangeWallet, ExternalWallet, ManualVenue.
`venue`: Bitunix, Manual. `syncMode`: Api, Manual.
A venue no API reaches. Holdings, transfers and balance snapshots for it are recorded by hand so the equity curve stays whole.

exec: // Names are unique per user, so keep re-runs from colliding (409).

request.description:
Credentials are write-only: they go in and never come back out.

The key is verified against Bitunix before it is stored, so a typo fails here rather than silently killing the sync loop later. Stored AES-GCM encrypted, with the encryption key in configuration rather than the database.

**Use a read-only key.** TradeLedger never places orders.
Detaches the key and stops automatic syncing for this account. Trades already imported are kept.

item.name: Trades
item.description: The journal itself: synced and manual trades, plus the review inbox.

request.description:
The journal, newest first, with paging and filters. Every query parameter is optional.

Saves the first result to `{{tradeId}}`.

Closed trades that still need their subjective half: strategy, mental state, checklist, mistakes, rating.

This is the queue to work through after the market closes.
The complete journal row including individual fills, tagged mistakes and trackings, resolved taxonomy names, and attachments.

exec: // Fall back to the first existing account so this request works on its own.

request.description:
For venues no API reaches: external wallets, other exchanges, on-chain swaps.

Gross PnL is derived from the prices you enter, then net PnL, outcome, achieved R and duration are computed the same way as for a synced trade.

`side`: Long, Short.

  "strategyId": "{{strategyId}}",
  "rating": 4,

  "tag": "clean-setup",
  "postTradeTag": "followed-plan",

  "mistakeIds": ["{{mistakeId}}"],

request.description:
Supplies what the exchange cannot know. Only the fields you send are changed, so a re-sync never wipes journalling.

Setting a stop loss here also recomputes achieved R, since a synced trade has no stop reported by the exchange. Pass `markReviewed` to clear it from the inbox.

Run **Journal > List strategies** and **List mistakes** first to populate `{{strategyId}}` and `{{mistakeId}}`. Returns the full trade with names resolved.

exec: // Fetch a taxonomy id only when the variable is not already set, so this
// request works on its own and in any Collection Runner order.

request.description: Manual trades only. A synced trade cannot be deleted: it would reappear on the next sync sweep, and deleting it would discard the journalling attached to it. Returns 409 if you try.

item.name: Plans
item.description: Pre-trade plans and the position-size calculator.

request.description:
The workbook Calculator sheet as an endpoint, and stateless: sizing a trade should not require committing to it.

Sizes the position so a stop-out loses exactly the risk budget, fees included, then reports order value, margin, take profit at the requested R multiple, and estimated profit and loss net of fees.

`riskFraction` is a fraction, so 0.01 is 1% of balance. Side is inferred from where the stop sits relative to entry.
Pre-trade plans, newest first, optionally filtered by status.

request.description:
Records intent before entry. Sizing is calculated and stored alongside.

When a matching fill arrives from Bitunix the plan is linked automatically and the trade is flagged planned. Plans expire after three days by default so an untaken plan stops competing to match some later, unrelated trade in the same symbol.
Marks a plan as not taken so it stops competing for matches. A plan already linked to a trade cannot be abandoned and returns 409.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Performance metrics, equity curve, drawdown and breakdowns. Every endpoint takes the same optional filters.

request.description:
Win rate, gross and net PnL, fees, funding, average win and loss, profit factor, expectancy, planned versus unplanned performance, streaks and average duration.

Profit factor is null rather than infinite when there are no losing trades yet.

Built from balance snapshots, never from summing trades, because spot bags, LP positions and transfers do not appear there.

Returns the curve plus peak equity, max drawdown with the date it happened, and current drawdown.

Slices closed trades by one dimension.

Allowed values: Strategy, Symbol, Side, Timeframe, MarketSession, EntryMentalState, ExitMentalState, DayOfWeek, HourOfDay, Planned.
The discipline metric: does having a plan before entry actually change the outcome?
Performance grouped by how the trader felt at entry.

How often each tagged mistake occurred and what it cost, ordered worst first.

Uses the explicitly attributed cost where one was given, otherwise the net result of the trades the mistake was tagged on.

item.name: Sync
item.description: Bitunix sync status, manual triggers and historical backfill. Every write is idempotent, so re-running is always safe.

request.description: Per account and endpoint: when it last synced, the timestamp of the newest record persisted, and whether the historical backfill has finished.
The last fifty sync attempts with records seen, records written, requests made and any error, so a silently stalled sync is visible.

Forces an incremental reconcile sweep for one account rather than waiting for the scheduled run.

Writes are idempotent, so running this repeatedly is safe and is a no-op when nothing is new.

Walks Bitunix history back to the account `trackedFrom` date. Run once after attaching credentials.

Safe to re-run: every write is an upsert keyed on the exchange position id.

Reads the Bitunix futures wallet and records an equity point.

Bonus is excluded from equity because it is not withdrawable and would inflate the curve.
Returns ok when the API is up. No authentication required.
